# Autoregressive Models

## Sequential Generation

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}autoregressive_overview.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Predict one element at a time, conditioned on all previous elements (@torralba_foundations_2024).
:::


## Factorization

::: {.fragment}
$$p(x_1, \ldots, x_n) = p(x_1)\, p(x_2|x_1)\, p(x_3|x_1, x_2) \cdots p(x_n|x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
Each conditional $p(x_i \mid x_1, \ldots, x_{i-1})$ is modeled by a neural network (masked CNN or Transformer).
:::

::: {.fragment}
> Image generation becomes a **sequence prediction problem.**
:::


## Sampling Step by Step

::: {.incremental}
1. Sample $x_1 \sim p(x_1)$
2. Sample $x_2 \sim p(x_2 \mid x_1)$
3. Sample $x_3 \sim p(x_3 \mid x_1, x_2)$
4. … continue until all pixels are generated
:::



## Pros & Cons

::: {.fragment}
**Pros**

- Exact likelihood computation
- Natural fit for language / discrete tokens
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Cons**

- Sequential generation is slow
- Pixel-level image generation is expensive
- Errors can accumulate during sampling
:::


# Generative Adversarial Networks

## The Adversarial Game

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}gan-architecture.jpg){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Generator $g(\vect{z})$ fakes — Discriminator $d(\vect{x})$ judges (@goodfellow_generative_2014).
:::


## Minimax Objective

::: {.fragment}
$$\min_{g} \max_{d} \mathbb{E}_{\vect{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log d(\vect{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\vect{z} \sim p_z}[\log(1 - d(g(\vect{z})))]$$
:::

::: {.incremental}
- $d$: maximize correct real/fake classification
- $g$: minimize $d$'s success — fool the discriminator
- Training **alternates** between the two
:::


## GAN Learning Process

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}gan_learning.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Generator distribution tries to fool discriminator, while discriminator must distinguish real from fake (@foster_generative_2023).
:::


## Pros & Cons

::: {.fragment}
**Pros**

- Fast sampling, one forward pass
- Can produce sharp images
- Historically pivotal for image generation
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Cons**

- Training can be unstable
- **Mode collapse**, limited variety
- No direct likelihood
- Modern text-to-image systems are rarely pure GANs
:::


# Variational Autoencoders

## VAE Architecture

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}vae_illustration.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
**Encoder** $q_{\psi}(\vect{z} \mid \vect{x})$ — **Decoder** $p_{\theta}(\vect{x} \mid \vect{z})$
:::


## Probabilistic Twist

::: {.fragment}
Unlike standard autoencoders, the latent space is **structured probabilistically**, so random samples decode to meaningful outputs.
:::


## Reparameterization Trick

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}vae_illustration2.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
$$\vect{z} = \vect{\mu} + \vect{\epsilon} \cdot \vect{\sigma}, \qquad \vect{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
Lets gradients flow through stochastic sampling.
:::


## ELBO Objective

::: {.fragment}
$$\text{ELBO} = \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\vect{z} \sim q_{\psi}(\vect{z}|\vect{x})}[\log p_{\theta}(\vect{x}|\vect{z})]}_{\text{Reconstruction}} - \underbrace{\text{KL}(q_{\psi}(\vect{z}|\vect{x}) \,\|\, p(\vect{z}))}_{\text{Regularization}}$$
:::

::: {.incremental}
- **Reconstruction** — decoder must recover the input
- **KL regularization** — pull posterior toward prior $p(\vect{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$
- Result: a **smooth, continuous** latent space
:::


## VAE Latent Space

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}vae_latent_space_face.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Traversing the latent space → smooth interpolation between faces (@prince_understanding_2023).
:::


## Pros & Cons

::: {.fragment}
**Pros**

- Principled probabilistic foundation
- Structured, interpretable latent space (interpolation, factor analysis)
- Stable training
- Useful for representation learning
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Cons**

- Tend to produce blurry outputs (improvable with more complex variants)
:::


# Diffusion Models


## Forward Diffusion

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}forward_diffusion_fcv.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Gradually add Gaussian noise over $T$ steps (@torralba_foundations_2024). **Fixed**, no neural network.
:::


## Forward Process

::: {.fragment}
$$\vect{x}_t = \sqrt{1 - \beta_t}\, \vect{x}_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta_t}\, \vect{\epsilon}_t, \qquad \vect{\epsilon}_t \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$$
:::

::: {.incremental}
- $\beta_t$ — **noise schedule** (linear, cosine, …)
- $\vect{x}_0$ (clean) → $\vect{x}_T \approx \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$
- Can sample $\vect{x}_t$ **directly from** $\vect{x}_0$ → efficient training over many noise levels
:::


## Reverse Diffusion

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}reverse_diffusion_fcv.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
A neural network learns to gradually remove noise, step by step (@torralba_foundations_2024).
:::


## Reverse Process

::: {.fragment}
Start from pure noise:
$$\vect{x}_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
Iteratively denoise to a realistic sample $\vect{x}_0$.
:::

::: {.fragment}
The network is **conditioned on the timestep $t$** — noise level varies dramatically across steps.
:::


## Training Objective

::: {.fragment}
$$\mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_{t, \vect{x}_0, \vect{\epsilon}}\left[\,\|\, \vect{\epsilon} - f_\theta(\vect{x}_t, t)\,\|^2\,\right]$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
The model predicts the **noise** $\vect{\epsilon}$ that was added to $\vect{x}_0$ to produce $\vect{x}_t$.
:::


## Training & Sampling

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}diffusion_algorithm.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Training: random $t$, random $\vect{\epsilon}$. Sampling: iterate from $T$ down to $0$.
:::


## U-Net Denoiser

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}diffusion_unet.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Encoder–decoder with skip connections; timestep $t$ embedded throughout (@prince_understanding_2023).
:::


## Pros & Cons

::: {.fragment}
**Pros**

- High-quality, diverse outputs (currently SOTA)
- Stable, reliable training
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Cons**

- Slow inference — iterative sampling
- High compute cost (training **and** inference)
:::


## Aside: Cold Diffusion

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}cold_diffusion.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Gaussian noise isn't fundamental — any **invertible degradation** works (blur, masking, pixelation) (@bansal_cold_2022).
:::

::: {.fragment}
Success comes from the **gradual, multi-step inversion**, not the noise itself.
:::


# Conditioning Across Families

## From $p(\vect{x})$ to $p(\vect{x} \mid \vect{c})$

::: {.fragment}
So far: model $p(\vect{x})$ unconditionally.
:::

::: {.fragment}
In practice: model
$$p_\theta(\vect{x} \mid \vect{c})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$\vect{c}$ — class label, text prompt, source image, mask, layout, depth, reference…
:::


## Conditioning Is Not a Separate Family

| Family | How conditioning enters |
|---|---|
| Autoregressive | condition each prediction step on $\vect{c}$ |
| VAEs | condition encoder and/or decoder on $\vect{c}$ |
| GANs | condition generator (and often discriminator) on $\vect{c}$ |
| Diffusion | condition the **denoising network** on $\vect{c}$ |

::: {.fragment}
Modern text-to-image and image-editing systems use these mechanisms extensively.
:::


## Recap {.center}

::: {.incremental}
- **Autoregressive** — exact likelihood, slow sequential sampling
- **GAN** — fast & sharp, unstable, mode collapse risk
- **VAE** — structured latent, stable, blurrier
- **Diffusion** — SOTA quality, iterative & costly
- **Conditioning** — applies to *all* of them
:::
